documentation.rationale: Searches `official Microsoft/Azure documentation`, `Microsoft Learn and other official sources`; the advertised outputs are first-party `article title, URL, and ... content excerpt`, not attacker-controlled or private user data.

azd.rationale: Advertises Azure Developer CLI operations for `resource provisioning, deployment, and monitoring`, which can reach non-public Azure resources under the user's credentials. Child commands and returned fields are not specified, so scope is partly undetermined.

foundry.rationale: Can `read, create, modify resources such as Models, Agents and Evaluation workflows in Microsoft Foundry platform`, so it can read non-public SaaS/resource data with the user's credentials and write/modify resources. Child command details are hidden.

get_azure_bestpractices.rationale: Returns `best practices for code generation, operations and deployment` and `AI application best practices`; this is guidance content, not private account data or attacker-controlled content.

aks.rationale: Requires `Azure subscription context` and provides subscription-scoped visibility into AKS `metadata—including Azure resource IDs, networking endpoints, identity configuration, and provisioning state`, which is non-public Azure account data. It says `Not for kubectl execution` or lifecycle changes, so treated as read-only.

appconfig.rationale: Manages Azure App Configuration stores and `key-value settings`, including `retrieving configuration data`; configuration data in the user's Azure account is non-public. It can also set labels and lock/unlock settings.

applens.rationale: Diagnoses `Azure resource issues` and detects problems/root causes for resources, so it can return private diagnostic data. Diagnostics may include error or behavior data influenced by external requests; the description does not exclude attacker-authored diagnostic/log text, so UNTRUSTED is kept as undetermined.

appservice.rationale: Can manage Azure App Service `web apps, databases, and configurations`, which are non-public account resources and can be changed. Subcommands and output fields are not specified.

role.rationale: Manages Azure RBAC resources, including `listing role assignments`, `managing permissions`, and access management `at various scopes`, exposing private authorization data and allowing writes.

datadog.rationale: Retrieves monitored Azure resource information and `health status` through a Datadog integration, which can reveal non-public monitoring/account data. Only listing/retrieval is advertised.

managedlustre.rationale: Can `create, update, list and inspect` Azure Managed Lustre file systems in the user's Azure account, exposing private resource data and enabling writes.

azuremigrate.rationale: Supports `policy and governance changes`, identity/subscription design, and can `generate a complete platform landing zone`; this can change Azure governance resources and may read non-public subscription design. Details are not fully specified.

azureterraformbestpractices.rationale: Returns `Terraform best practices for Azure`; no private data, attacker-controlled source, or write is advertised.

deploy.rationale: Provides commands for `deploying applications to Azure` and can `fetch application logs`, so it can change Azure state and return private app data. Application logs may contain attacker-controlled request/content text; the description does not rule that out.

deviceregistry.rationale: Can `manage Azure Device Registry resources` and supports `listing namespaces` and managing resources in `your Azure subscription`, exposing private subscription data and enabling writes.

eventgrid.rationale: Manages and accesses Event Grid `topics, domains, and event subscriptions`, which are private Azure resources. Event subscriptions commonly designate delivery endpoints; because the child schema is hidden, the description does not exclude an agent-chosen endpoint, so SINK is kept as undetermined.

acr.rationale: Manages Azure Container Registry resources and `registry configurations`, exposing private registry metadata and enabling configuration changes.

advisor.rationale: Requires `Azure subscription context` and provides subscription-scoped Advisor recommendations, which are non-public account data. Only manage/query recommendations are advertised; no external sink.

bicepschema.rationale: Retrieves Bicep `schemas, templates, and resource definitions` for IaC support; the advertised source is schema/template knowledge, not private user data or attacker-authored content.

cosmos.rationale: Manages and queries Azure Cosmos DB `accounts, databases, containers, and document queries`, which can expose private database data and change resources. Query results may include multi-writer/app data; the description does not exclude attacker-authored documents, so UNTRUSTED is undetermined.

cloudarchitect.rationale: Generates Azure architecture `designs and recommendations based on requirements`; no account read, attacker-controlled output source, or state change is advertised.

communication.rationale: Manages Azure Communication Services and `supports sending SMS`; SMS sends agent-supplied content to agent-chosen recipients, a SINK, and resource management can expose private Azure account data.

compute.rationale: Can `list, query, create, or monitor VMs and VMSS instances` and access only resources available to the authenticated user, exposing private compute metadata and enabling VM creation/management.

confidentialledger.rationale: Can append and query `tamper-proof ledger entries`; ledger contents are non-public account data, and `write immutable audit records` changes state.

containerapps.rationale: Manages Azure Container Apps resources and `container app configurations`, exposing private account resource metadata and allowing changes.

eventhubs.rationale: Manages Event Hubs namespaces and event hubs and includes `CRUD operations`, so it can read and change private Azure messaging resources.

fileshares.rationale: `Commands for managing Azure File Shares` can expose and change non-public file share resources. Child commands and content access are unspecified.

foundryextensions.rationale: Interacts with Foundry OpenAI, `knowledge indexes, threads, agents, and resources`, exposing private SaaS/resource data and allowing interaction/management. Threads or knowledge indexes may contain third-party text; the description does not exclude attacker-authored content.

functionapp.rationale: Manages and accesses Azure Function App resources, which are non-public Azure account resources, and management implies state changes.

functions.rationale: Provides Azure Functions `code generation commands`, language/runtime exploration, and templates; no private account data or attacker-controlled source is advertised.

grafana.rationale: Manages and accesses Azure Managed Grafana resources and `monitoring dashboards`, which can contain non-public monitoring data and can be changed.

keyvault.rationale: `managing and accessing Azure Key Vault resources` can return non-public secrets/keys/certificates and modify vault resources.

kusto.rationale: Can execute `KQL queries` and manage Azure Data Explorer clusters/databases, exposing private analytics data and allowing management. Query results may include attacker-controlled telemetry or multi-writer data; not excluded by the description.

loadtesting.rationale: Manages Azure Load Testing resources and can configure scripts and `executing performance tests`; tests send traffic to configured targets, so hidden parameters may choose attacker-readable URLs/hosts. Test resources/results are private account data.

marketplace.rationale: Manages/accesses Azure Marketplace `products and offers`; Marketplace product/offer text can be authored by third-party publishers, so it is UNTRUSTED. `managing` Marketplace resources may expose account/private offer data or change state, but details are not specified.

quota.rationale: Checks Azure resource `quota and usage` for resource types/regions, exposing non-public subscription usage. No state change is advertised.

monitor.rationale: Queries and analyzes Azure Monitor `logs and metrics`, exposing private monitoring data. Logs may contain attacker-controlled request/message text; the description does not exclude that.

applicationinsights.rationale: Lists and manages Application Insights components, private Azure resources. It explicitly says these commands `do not support querying metrics or logs`, so no log-content UNTRUSTED label is inferred.

mysql.rationale: Manages Azure Database for MySQL and executes `SQL queries`, exposing private database data and allowing configuration changes. Query rows may include app/multi-writer attacker-authored data; not excluded.

policy.rationale: Can `Manage Azure Policy assignments and definitions`, retrieve assignments, and analyze compliance, exposing private governance/compliance data and enabling writes.

postgres.rationale: Manages PostgreSQL resources and executes `SQL queries`, exposing private database data and allowing configuration changes. Query results may contain attacker-authored app data; not excluded.

pricing.rationale: Gets `Azure retail pricing for SKUs, services, regions`; this is public vendor pricing data and no state change or attacker-authored source is advertised.

redis.rationale: Lists Redis resources, databases, data access policies and can create Azure Managed Redis resources, exposing private account metadata and allowing writes.

resourcehealth.rationale: Monitors and diagnoses Azure `resource health`, `availability status`, and service health events for the user's resources, exposing private operational data. No writes are advertised.

search.rationale: Can manage and query Azure AI Search `services, indexes, and knowledge sources` and supports `document search`; search indexes/documents may contain private data and may include attacker-authored documents. Management implies writes.

speech.rationale: Works with Speech STT/TTS, audio processing, and language detection. It sends supplied audio/text to a fixed Azure AI Services endpoint, but the text does not advertise reading private files/accounts or sending to attacker-chosen destinations.

servicebus.rationale: Manages Azure Service Bus `queues, topics, and subscriptions`, private Azure messaging resources, and management changes state. The description does not advertise receiving or sending message bodies to external recipients.

servicefabric.rationale: Provides visibility into Service Fabric managed cluster nodes including `node status, node types, IP addresses, and fault/upgrade domains`, which is private subscription data. No state-changing operation is described.

signalr.rationale: Manages Azure SignalR Service resources and lists services, exposing private account resources and potentially changing them via management commands.

sql.rationale: Manages Azure SQL `databases, servers, and elastic pools`, including firewall rules and Entra ID administrators, exposing private account configuration and allowing writes. It does not advertise querying table data.

storage.rationale: Can create/list/get/manage Storage accounts, containers, blobs and tables and `upload files to blob storage`; this exposes private storage account/blob metadata and changes Azure Storage state. The description does not state blobs are public or attacker-readable.

storagesync.rationale: Manages Azure File Sync resources, sync groups, endpoints, and registered servers, exposing private hybrid storage configuration and allowing deployment/maintenance writes.

virtualdesktop.rationale: Manages and accesses Azure Virtual Desktop `hostpools, session hosts, and user sessions`, exposing private desktop/session information and allowing management writes.

wellarchitectedframework.rationale: Accesses Azure Well-Architected Framework `guidance, best practices, and recommendations`; no private account access, attacker-controlled source, or state change is advertised.

workbooks.rationale: Can list, create, update, and delete Azure Workbooks and manage workbook `configurations and content`, exposing private dashboard resources and allowing writes.

group_list.rationale: Lists all resource groups in a subscription and returns resource group `names and IDs`, which are non-public Azure account metadata. Annotation says read-only.

group_resource_list.rationale: Lists all resources in a specified resource group and returns resource `names, IDs, types, and locations`, private subscription metadata. Annotation says read-only.

subscription_list.rationale: Lists all Azure subscriptions for the current account and returns `subscriptionId, displayName, state, tenantId, and isDefault`, which is non-public account/tenant data. Annotation says read-only.

extension_azqr.rationale: Runs Azure Quick Review CLI to generate `compliance and security reports for Azure resources` and returns the generated `report file path`; this reaches private subscription/resource configuration. It writes a report file, but the advertised command is azqr-specific, not arbitrary host execution.

extension_cli_generate.rationale: Generates Azure CLI commands for a supplied `intent`; it returns generated instructions/commands and does not execute them, read private data, or contact an agent-chosen destination.

extension_cli_install.rationale: Provides installation instructions for CLI tools; no private data access, attacker-controlled source, write, or execution is advertised.

notes: All hierarchical router tools expose only generic `command` and `parameters` schemas; where the description advertises management/write capabilities but not child schemas, destination_args/value_args are limited to those declared generic arguments and undetermined is set when exact reach or output fields are not settled.

A query or operation against fixed Microsoft/Azure service endpoints is not treated as a SINK unless the advertised capability can deliver data to an agent-chosen recipient, URL, or host, such as SMS, Event Grid subscriptions, or load-test targets.
